name: 225. MCP tool auto-injection scope: off by default, opt-in header, and the auto-inject window (mcp-tool-injection) [SERIAL]
description:
The harness profile sets mcp.tool_manager_config.disable_auto_tool_inject: true, so the sse_mcp fixture (examples/mcps/remote-test-server on :3012) no longer adds echo/add/greet and its server instructions to every chat and responses request: before that, ~190 unrelated rows saw tools and a system message they never sent. disable_auto_tool_inject is gateway-wide (core/mcp/toolmanager.go ParseAndAddToolsToRequest), there is no per-client or per-virtual-key switch, and governance only stamps a virtual key's tool list when auto-injection is on or an include-clients header is present. So this folder is the auto-injection scope: a [SERIAL] window that flips the flag on through PUT /api/config, with nothing else running against the gateway, and restores it.

Three scopes are pinned, chat and responses each: (c) the default scope without an MCP header gets no sse_mcp tool and no server instructions on the provider wire (the regression pin for the profile change, asserted before the window and again after the restore); (b) x-bf-mcp-include-clients: sse_mcp opts one request in while auto-injection is off; (a) with auto-injection on, a request with no MCP header gets the tools and the instructions, and the auto-executable echo tool runs server side. Wire rows send tool_choice none so the single upstream turn is the one asserted; run rows assert the final upstream turn carries the echo tool's result ({"echoed": ...}) and the answer carries the echoed token. Provider-level injected_tools (folder 198) resolve independently of this flag (core/injectedtools.go) and are not covered here.
